primaryText: If I go to London, my sister will pick me up at the airport.
comment: The paradigm conditional presupposition: Strong Kleene and Karttunen and Peters (p. 51), and the CCP of ABLE (p. 248), predict only 'if I go to London I have a sister'; hearers infer the stronger 'I have a sister', which Ch. 9 derives as an implicature over information orderings.

primaryText: If Spaceman Spiff lands on Planet X, he will be bothered by the fact that his weight is greater than it would be on Earth.
paperFeatures: the fact that + factive bothered by
comment: Presupposes only the conditional: if he lands there, his weight is greater. Natural when Spiff hangs weightless in space, so the unconditional presupposition is wrong; structural accommodation accounts cannot produce the conditional reading.

primaryText: It is unlikely that if Spaceman Spiff lands on Planet X, he will be bothered by the fact that his weight is greater than it would be on Earth.
paperFeatures: the fact that + factive bothered by
comment: Preferred reading keeps the conditional implication; accommodation into the consequent yields 'it is unlikely that if he lands his weight will be greater and he will be bothered by it', which lacks that implication.

primaryText: If Spaceman Spiff lands on Planet X and is bothered by the fact that his weight is greater than it would be on Earth, he won't stay long.
paperFeatures: the fact that + factive bothered by
comment: Same conditional presupposition, predicted by the treatment of conjunction; accommodation into the consequent is not even available.

primaryText: Anna realises that Bertha is hiding.
comment: §6.5 translation: the presupposition that Bertha is hiding conjoined with the assertion that Anna has come to believe it.

primaryText: Anna does not realise that Bertha is hiding.
comment: A negated formula carries the same presuppositions as its positive counterpart.

primaryText: If Anna realises that Bertha is hiding, then she will find her.
Anna might realise that Bertha is hiding.
Bertha regrets that Anna realises that she is hiding.
comment: NVB_B_(∂_bih&cb_a_bih) is the atom that Bertha has negative vibes arising from her belief that Anna realises she is hiding.

primaryText: If Bertha is not in the kitchen, then Anna realises that Bertha is in the attic.
comment: The book's translation writes bc for 'Bertha is in the kitchen'. Only the conditionalised presupposition is entailed (E175d), the standard weak CCP prediction.

primaryText: If Bertha is hiding, then Anna realises that Bertha is hiding.
Perhaps Bertha is hiding and Anna realises that Bertha is hiding.
comment: Every information state admits the translation, so the sentence carries no presupposition.

primaryText: It is possible there is a happy farmer, but, then again, it is possible that there are no happy farmers.
paperFeatures: might phi and might not phi
comment: Consistent as a might-sequence; following it with E207a is consistent, while E207a followed by E206a is not — might is a consistency test on the current state.
Order contrast with E206a: assertion then might-sentence is inconsistent, might-sentence then assertion is fine.
